INTEGRATED SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Laboratory apparatus and instruments? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory apparatus and instruments.

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.

5. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Glucose and oxygen

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Primary consumers only

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids, Bases and Indicators? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids, Bases and Indicators.

8. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. newton (N)
   D. pascal (Pa)

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Magnetism? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Magnetism.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Magnetism.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Magnetism.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Magnetism.

11. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

12. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Reproductive System? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproductive System.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Reproductive System.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Reproductive System.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Human Reproductive System.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Excretory System? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Excretory System.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Human Excretory System.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Excretory System.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Excretory System.

15. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

16. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Removing all vegetation

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Electrical Energy and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Magnetism and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Integrated Science and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Laboratory Safety and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Laboratory apparatus and instruments and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Mixtures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
